svg.title: Control the Vehicle-to-Cash Chain
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-vehicle-to-settlement-workflow; chart type: process_flow; title: Control the Vehicle-to-Cash Chain; subtitle: Five operating steps for investor vehicles, qualified drivers, and reconciled collections.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The asset-light model assumes documented owner authority and platform acceptance of each vehicle and arrangement. Gross operator billings mean driver leases, dispatch, and co-hosting charges; passenger trip GMV and investor vehicle values remain outside this revenue measure.; caption: A top-of-waterfall lease is a contractual collection priority, not an automatic platform capability. Use Uber fleet settlement features only where the account supports the documented split; otherwise reconcile authorized collections separately.; stages: label: Secure vehicle authority; value: Document ownership and permitted commercial use before listing; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Capture VIN, title or lease authority, lender restrictions, owner settlement terms, and responsibility for depreciation. Reject vehicles whose financing or insurance excludes the intended rental, livery, or rideshare activity.; label: Qualify driver and operation; value: Match driver credentials to vehicle and service jurisdiction; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Verify applicable licenses, platform eligibility, MVR authorization, inspection dates, airport access, and policy endorsements. Treat personal use, app-on waiting, accepted trips, and passenger carriage as distinct exposure states.; label: Execute handover and collection; value: Record condition and activate expressly authorized payment instructions; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Photograph condition, record odometer and fuel, explain deductibles and toll charges, and obtain the required payment authorization. Keep refundable security deposits in a liability ledger rather than recording them as sales.; label: Monitor service and exceptions; value: Convert telematics exceptions into scheduled human operating decisions; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use OBD-II GPS, diagnostic alerts, and maintenance mileage to schedule service. Route collision, overdue-payment, and vehicle-location exceptions to a named operator. Never remotely interrupt a moving or occupied vehicle.; label: Close weekly settlements; value: Reconcile billed charges, collected cash, and owner distributions; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Match Uber settlement exports, authorized ACH receipts, toll statements, repair invoices, and owner splits to vehicle-level ledgers. Age failed collections separately and reconcile retained contribution before calculating profit.

circle.title: label: Secure vehicle authority; value: Document ownership and permitted commercial use before listing; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Capture VIN, title or lease authority, lender restrictions, owner settlement terms, and responsibility for depreciation. Reject vehicles whose financing or insurance excludes the intended rental, livery, or rideshare activity.

Treat personal use, app-on waiting, accepted trips, and passenger carriage as distinct exposure states.

circle.title: label: Execute handover and collection; value: Record condition and activate expressly authorized payment instructions; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Photograph condition, record odometer and fuel, explain deductibles and toll charges, and obtain the required payment authorization. Keep refundable security deposits in a liability ledger rather than recording them as sales.

circle.title: label: Monitor service and exceptions; value: Convert telematics exceptions into scheduled human operating decisions; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use OBD-II GPS, diagnostic alerts, and maintenance mileage to schedule service. Route collision, overdue-payment, and vehicle-location exceptions to a named operator. Never remotely interrupt a moving or occupied vehicle.

Age failed collections separately and reconcile retained contribution before calculating profit.

Assumptions: The asset-light model assumes documented owner authority and platform acceptance of each vehicle and arrangement. Gross operator billings mean driver leases, dispatch, and co-hosting charges; passenger trip GMV and investor vehicle values remain outside this revenue measure.
